newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Chamorro invites region's president to farewell.
newsitem.headline: Chamorro invites region's president to farewell.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Violeta Chamorro on Monday invited Central America's presidents to Managua for a farewell meeting on December 2.
Chamorro, who will leave office on January 10, came to power in 1990 after her surprise election victory over former left-wing Sandinista President Daniel Ortega.

"The Central American presidents that I have invited to bid me farewell will meet here soon, and from this moment all are invited," Chamorro said after receiving a recognition plaque from Nicaragua's largest private business group.
She said invitations had been extended to the presidents of Guatemala, Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras and Panama.
Chamorro, 68, the widow of a slain newspaper publisher, inherited a country economically and politically shattered by eight years of civil war and a U.S.-backed economic embargo.
She said her proudest accomplishments were bringing peace, reconciliation and democracy to Nicaragua after decades of dictatorship and two bloody civil wars.
"For the first time in more than 100 years of our history, one democratically elected president is going to hand over power to another," she said.
She also called for national reconciliation and an end to a lingering post-election squabble in which the Sandinista Front has appealed the results of the October 20 vote as fraudulent.

Almost one month after the vote, an official winner has still not been announced, even though Arnoldo Aleman of the Liberal Alliance has already proclaimed himself winner and received the congratulations of the world leaders.
